content: The clinical interaction studies of famciclovir with cimetidine did not reveal any significant effects on the formation of penciclovir. Felbamate increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by influencing the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Similarly, felodipine also increases cimetidine levels or effects via CYP2C19 metabolism, with unknown significance. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism, but the clinical relevance remains uncertain. Fluconazole raises cimetidine levels or effects through CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of fluphenazine, flurbiprofen, fluvastatin, and ibuprofen (including IV formulations) by affecting various hepatic enzymes (CYP2D6, CYP2C9/10), though the significance is unclear. It also increases the levels or effects of green tea by influencing CYP1A2 metabolism, which may inhibit caffeine metabolism. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of loratadine, losartan, and modafinil by affecting CYP2D6 or CYP2C19 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. For losartan, cimetidine may inhibit its conversion to the active metabolite E-3174, necessitating monitoring of therapeutic response. Cimetidine increases ospemifene levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while oxcarbazepine and parecoxib increase cimetidine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, with unclear significance. Pentobarbital and phenobarbital decrease cimetidine levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of perhexiline, perphenazine, prochlorperazine, promazine, and promethazine by influencing CYP2D6 metabolism, with unclear significance. It also increases ramelteon levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Rifampin decreases cimetidine levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Cimetidine increases riluzole levels via CYP1A2 metabolism and risperidone levels via CYP2D6 metabolism, with unclear significance. It also increases sulfamethoxazole and tolterodine levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP2D6 metabolism, respectively. Cimetidine raises trifluoperazine and tropisetron levels via CYP2D6 metabolism, with unclear significance. It increases varenicline levels by reducing renal clearance. Voriconazole increases cimetidine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, while cimetidine raises voriconazole levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Acalabrutinib increases cimetidine levels through other mechanisms, while cimetidine decreases acalabrutinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases with higher gastric pH, so it should be administered two hours before H2-receptor antagonists. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of alfentanil, alfuzosin, and alosetron by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. For alosetron, cimetidine also affects CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Cimetidine increases alprazolam and amiodarone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs are recommended. Amitriptyline levels are increased by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Amobarbital decreases cimetidine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Cimetidine increases amphetamine and antipyrine levels via CYP2D6 and CYP1A2 metabolism, respectively. Apalutamide decreases cimetidine levels by increasing elimination, and caution is advised. Cimetidine increases aprepitant and aripiprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, with alternative drugs recommended. Armodafinil increases cimetidine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, while cimetidine raises armodafinil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Cimetidine increases artemether/lumefantrine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs are advised. It raises asenapine levels via CYP1A2 metabolism. Atazanavir levels are affected by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism and increased gastric pH, requiring alternative drugs. Atogepant and atomoxetine levels are increased by cimetidine via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism, respectively. Cimetidine increases atorvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs are recommended. Avanafil levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments. Avapritinib levels are also increased by cimetidine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Axitinib levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring close monitoring or alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases azelastine levels by decreasing metabolism. It raises bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs are recommended. Cimetidine increases bendamustine levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism, reducing active metabolite concentrations. Benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP2D6 metabolism, affecting hydromorphone formation. Berotralstat increases cimetidine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Cimetidine raises bexarotene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Blessed thistle decreases cimetidine effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Cimetidine increases bortezomib and bosentan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor effects on bosentan through CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Bosutinib increases cimetidine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, while cimetidine raises bosutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Brexpiprazole levels are increased by cimetidine through CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring dose adjustments. Budesonide levels are affected by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism and increased gastric pH, necessitating alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases buprenorphine levels by decreasing metabolism, and alternative drugs are recommended. It raises buspirone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Butabarbital and butalbital decrease cimetidine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Cimetidine increases butorphanol levels by decreasing metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cimetidine raises cabazitaxel and cabozantinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. It increases caffeine levels through CYP1A2 metabolism. Carbamazepine levels are raised by cimetidine through decreased metabolism, requiring plasma level monitoring. Cimetidine decreases carbonyl iron levels by increasing gastric pH. Cimetidine increases carmustine levels by decreasing metabolism, enhancing myelotoxicity. Carvedilol levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP2C9/10 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Cimetidine decreases cefdinir, cefditoren, cefpodoxime, and cefuroxime levels by increasing gastric pH. Celecoxib levels are increased by cimetidine via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Cimetidine raises cevimeline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. It increases chlordiazepoxide levels by decreasing metabolism. Chloroquine levels are raised by cimetidine through decreased metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases chlorpromazine levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Cimetidine raises cilostazol levels via CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cinacalcet levels are increased by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism. Cimetidine raises citalopram levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments to avoid QT prolongation. Cimetidine increases clarithromycin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Clomipramine levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Cimetidine increases clonazepam levels by decreasing metabolism. It reduces clopidogrel efficacy by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cimetidine raises clorazepate levels by decreasing metabolism. Clozapine levels are increased by cimetidine through CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cimetidine raises codeine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing its conversion to morphine. Cimetidine increases conivaptan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. It raises conjugated estrogens levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cimetidine decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility and bioavailability. Cimetidine decreases cyanocobalamin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Cyclosporine levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Cimetidine decreases dabrafenib levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility and bioavailability. Danicopan increases cimetidine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Darifenacin levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Darolutamide increases cimetidine levels through BCRP inhibition, necessitating alternative drugs. Cimetidine raises darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Dasatinib levels are affected by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism and increased gastric pH, requiring alternative drugs. Desipramine levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP2D6 metabolism. Devil's claw decreases cimetidine effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Dexamethasone levels are raised by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Dexmethylphenidate levels are increased by cimetidine through increased gastric pH. Cimetidine raises dextroamphetamine and dextromethorphan levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Diazepam levels are increased by cimetidine through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs.
